newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS - Options show mixed market signals.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS - Options show mixed market signals.

text.p: Trading in major U.S. index options this week has been flashing mixed signals to traders and analysts attempting to figure out when the market, down sharply, may recover from its slide.
On one hand, investors continued to buy a lot more S&P 100 index calls than puts, suggesting the fear factor was not high enough to touch off a rally.
But on the other hand, investors were buying more individual equity puts than calls and investor sentiment surveys were showing a solid drop in bullishness.
"The put-call ratios are confused," said Jay Shartsis, head of options trading at R.F. Lafferty & Co in New York.
"But there are enough measures that show a lot of fear that I think a good rally is at hand," he said. "I don't know whether it will be sustained. You're probably in a bear market."
Joseph Sunderman, an analyst at Investment Research Institute in Cincinnati, added that the Chicago Board Options Exchange's total put-call ratio has not reached levels that suggest a turnaround.
"Usually on these market cascades like we've had, you see put-call ratios approaching the 1.0 level where speculators are buying just as many puts as calls expecting to make a quick buck," he said.
"Right now we haven't even come close despite the market continuing to decline," he said.
At 1430 CST/2030 GMT, the CBOE's put-call ratio was 0.77.
At 1450 CST/2050 GMT, the OEX was down 1.35 points at 728.14, off its 722.36 session low.
The S&P 500 index fell 0.44 to 749.67. It had reached 744.40.
The bellwether Dow industrial average .DJI was off about 43 points at 6,474 after being down more than 95 points intraday. The Dow fell nearly 225 points in the first three days of this week.
Shartsis noted that while the Dow dropped Thursday, the technology-heavy Nasdaq composite index .IXIC was up solidly. The index was up 11.57 at 1,212.57 in late trade.
"I wouldn't ignore that," he aid. "It's a good positive divergence. It usually leads to a good rally."
He added that his dollar-weighted put-call ratio was high, indicating investors were concerned about the market's drop.
Shartsis said the March U.S. employment report, due out before the market open Friday, was one likely reason for the high fear factor.
He added the market could rally once the report is released.
Lawrence McMillan, who publishes the Daily Volume Alert, said in a report Thursday that the market was very oversold, which typically leads to strong "reflex" rallies.
"The bad news is that, once you get this oversold, the market can't just rally straight up -- it needs to rally and then retest the previous bottom," he said in the report.
